Theorem
[The Codazzi Equation] ↗ thm:gauss-equation 1. ch8:8.9

For all $W,X,Y\in \mathfrak X(M)$, egin{equation} (\widetilde R(W,X)Y)^\perp =( abla _W^F\mathrm{II})(X,Y)-( abla _X^F\mathrm{II})(W,Y). ag {8.6} \end{equation}

Proof

\sketch It suffices to pair both sides with an arbitrary normal field $N$:

egin{equation} \langle \widetilde R(W,X)Y,N angle =\langle ( abla _W^F\mathrm{II})(X,Y),N angle -\langle ( abla _X^F\mathrm{II})(W,Y),N angle . ag {8.7} \end{equation}

After applying the Gauss formula to the ambient curvature definition, retain only normal components. The first ambient derivative contributes

\[ \mathrm{II}(W, abla _XY) +( abla _W^F\mathrm{II})(X,Y) +\mathrm{II}( abla _WX,Y) +\mathrm{II}(X, abla _WY), \]

and the second contributes the analogous expression with $W,X$ interchanged, while the bracket term contributes $-\mathrm{II}([W,X],Y)$. The terms containing $ abla _XY$ and $ abla _WY$ cancel, and

\[ \mathrm{II}( abla _WX- abla _XW-[W,X],Y)=0 \]

by symmetry of $ abla $. Pairing the remaining terms with $N$ gives (8.7).

□
